facts.fact: The World Bank's aide-memoire of its mission of 17-21 November 2025 states that the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation has been supporting the development of civil registration and vital statistics with funding from the US Centers for Disease Control, and that the Bank's own project will support a transition strategy to keep CRVS operations running.

The World Bank's aide-memoire of its mission of 17-21 November 2025 states that the US CDC funding behind CRVS development was expected to be suspended in March 2026, and that the project would support a transition strategy, including an integrated NRIS-CRVS system within the National Registration Bureau, to ensure CRVS operations continue.

systems.owner: National Registration Bureau (NRB); development supported by the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation (EGPAF) with US CDC funding

systems.tiers: planned, to be established under the project's CRVS transition strategy

systems.system: ID Biometric Registration Kits for National Registration Bureau
systems.tiers: under procurement in November 2025 (about US$4m), intended to accelerate citizen enrolment and raise birth and death registration rates

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development

note: CRVS is classed civil on the document's description of it as the country's civil registration operations; the document does not say how or where a birth or death is entered, so there is no events, made or offices fact. The last12 fact rests on an anticipated suspension (March 2026), not one the document reports as having happened. Also stated, with no fact taken: a mapping of all NRB registration offices found critical gaps in infrastructure, connectivity and staffing (no counts), and a US$5m procurement of security paper for blank birth and death certificates was proposed for cancellation.
